overview: The Solid Waste Task Force hosted a public listening session to present a transition plan for Medford's waste collection system, including a shift to bi-weekly trash collection and weekly composting starting July 1, 2027. Dozens of residents spoke during the public comment period, with a vast majority expressing concern and opposition regarding the bi-weekly trash collection schedule.

items.title: Presentation on Proposed Waste System Changes
items.summary: City officials and waste consultants outlined the upcoming waste collection schedule changes, detailing environmental benefits, state waste bans, and a projected $13 million in municipal savings over eight years.

items.title: Public Comment on Trash Collection Reductions
items.summary: Numerous residents opposed the reduction to every-other-week trash collection due to concerns over pest infestations, pet waste, diaper sanitation, and equity for senior citizens, though a few participants spoke in support of composting goals.

items.title: Adjournment and Next Steps
items.summary: The public meeting adjourned with an announcement that the next public forum on waste collection changes would be held in person at Medford City Hall on January 28.

subject: Proposed Waste Collection System Transition
